title: Rome Wasn't Built in One Turn: Replay-Grounded Reward Signals for Long-Horizon Freeciv Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.41264v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training language-model agents to play long-horizon strategy games is hard because deterministic feedback is sparse and often arrives only at the end of a game. In-game scores can offer dense signals, but they do not reliably predict future outcomes: in 8-68% of position pairs across eight strategy games, the higher-scoring position leads to the worse outcome. We term this phenomenon scoreboard traps. In Freeciv, an open-source turn-based empire-building game where several players manage units, cities, and diplomacy over hundreds of turns, we look into better reward signals for gameplay agents. To facilitate this, we build CivHarness, an open system that saves current game states, branches on different decisions, and replays the game to future turns to provide measurable long-horizon feedback from saved positions. We use CivHarness to train CivTelescope, an LLM Judge that predicts which one of two game positions will yield the better out

translated_title: 罗马并非一回合建成：基于回放的长程Freeciv智能体奖励信号
translated_abstract: 训练语言模型智能体玩长程策略游戏十分困难，因为确定性反馈稀疏，且往往只在游戏结束时才能获得。游戏内分数虽然能提供密集的信号，但并不能可靠地预测未来结果：在八款策略游戏中的8-68%位置对里，得分较高的位置反而会导致更差的结果。我们将这种现象称为“记分板陷阱”。Freeciv是一款开源的回合制帝国建设游戏，多名玩家需要在数百个回合中管理单位、城市和外交。在该游戏中，我们研究了更适合游戏智能体的奖励信号。为此，我们构建了CivHarness——一个开放系统，它保存当前游戏状态、在不同决策处进行分支，并将游戏回放到未来回合，从而从保存的位置提供可测量的长程反馈。我们利用CivHarness训练了CivTelescope，一个LLM裁判，用于预测两个游戏位置中哪一个会产生更好的结果……
tldr: 针对策略游戏中“记分板陷阱”（高分不等于好结局）导致的奖励信号稀疏且不可靠问题，论文提出CivHarness回放系统，通过保存状态、分支决策并回放至未来回合，训练出能预测长程游戏结局的LLM裁判CivTelescope，为Freeciv智能体提供可靠的长程奖励信号。
en_tdlr: To overcome sparse and misleading rewards in long-horizon strategy games—where higher scores often lead to worse outcomes ("scoreboard traps")—this paper introduces CivHarness, a system that branches saved game states and replays them to future turns, and trains CivTelescope, an LLM judge that predicts which position yields the better outcome, providing grounded long-horizon reward signals for Freeciv agents.
